originality.rationale: The primary new statement optimizes Gaussian endpoint relative entropy variance at fixed forward KL and characterizes its full range and equality cases. Source [1] supplies the physical endpoint identity and qualitative variance motivation but not this frontier. Source [2] supplies a parallel dimension-independent reverse-KL extremization with similar Lambert roots, not the log-likelihood-variance objective. Full relevant primary sections, supplemental proofs, targeted literature and indexed scientific-result comparisons were compared by their mathematical implications, and no direct stronger result was identified. Remaining risk of an implicit general divergence-moment theorem is recorded.
residual_risks: A general information-spectrum or Gaussian quadratic-form extremal theorem not located may implicitly subsume the dimension-free range.

The Lambert roots and one-mode allocation have strong analogy with the known reverse-KL Gaussian theorem; the mathematical objective difference is substantive but reduces standalone novelty certainty.
The physical interpretation cannot be extended from exact-score, infinite-time endpoints to generic learned-score trajectories.

value.rationale: The motivating nonequilibrium interpretation makes the exact feasible fluctuation range at a prescribed average entropy production a natural, non-arbitrary physical and statistical question. The finding supplies both extrema, structural rigidity and all attainable intermediate variances in every Gaussian dimension, sharply bounding the diagnostic informativeness of a mean mismatch and characterizing its worst and best heterogeneity.
